agent_response.summary: Candidate 1 (4c12600) passed both the official check and the strict check in its full run: first run 22.495 s, against 23.840 s for the parent. Forward execution was 8.55 s and gradient execution 1.67 s; peak memory fell from 10.8 GB to 8.1 GB. All physical outputs matched the reference bit for bit. The largest normalized gradient error was 2.2e-6, with no failing entries. Candidate 2 adds an exact assembly change on top of candidate 1. The two fixed sideband blocks are now conjugated with slice updates, `SLICE_CONJUGATION = True` in `_assemble_signal_and_noise`, instead of a where-mask over the whole matrix. Setting the constant to False restores the old mask path. Notes now include candidate 1's runs and phase timings, and the operator proposals.
agent_response.hypothesis: Conjugating only the two fixed blocks by slice update gives the same values. The reverse pass only copies and conjugates, with no additions, so the gradient should match candidate 1 bit for bit. Inside the per-frequency assembly loop it avoids a whole-matrix conjugate-and-select and the mask construction, in both the forward and reverse passes. I expect a small saving of at most about 0.2 s, possibly within run-to-run noise. Nothing has been measured yet.
agent_response.notes: Best fully validated revision is candidate 1, 4c12600 (22.495 s; official and strict pass; one run, no paired repeat). If candidate 2 is not faster than 22.495 s, or fails the strict check, keep candidate 1 and set SLICE_CONJUGATION=False. Compile time did not change with candidate 1. The saving was in execution time and memory, which suggests the duplicate LU(A) and its residuals were not merged automatically before. That is an inference; the HLO was not inspected.
